content:
Tim Cook visits Apple's Battersea campus in London this week and meets King Charles, as part of a new partnership between Apple and the King's Trust.

At Apple's Battersea headquarters, Cook also sat down with The Independent for an in-depth interview, discussing the partnership and his first month as executive chairman of Apple.

Cook stepped down as CEO of Apple late last month, handing over the reins to John Ternus. In this week's interview, Cook noted that the handover had "actually begun several years ago."

Ternus takes over as CEO just as the iPhone Duo launch, with Cook stating that the product was already fully planned out. Cook explained: "I wanted to give John the wind at his back, and that wind at Apple is largely built on the product cycle."

Cook also stressed that as Apple's executive chairman, he is now focused on "global policy" matters, and mentioned that he has "an extremely high degree of mutual trust" with Ternus. Cook is assisting Ternus "in any way he sees fit," while also stating that he is "absolutely not interfering."

What advice did Cook give Ternus? "Don't try to be me." To read the full interview, head over to The Independent. The interview also has a fantastic discussion of Apple's latest partnership with the King's Trust.
